not_found: 801.5 nm quench line 4s[3/2]2-4p[5/2]2 (1s5-2p8): no measured frequency, isotope shift or A value beyond NIST located (the 800.8 nm line recorded here is the neighbouring 1s4-2p6 transition used for optical pumping).
Absolute optical frequency of 811.5 nm better than NIST: not located.
Experimental reduced matrix elements: none located.
Lifetime of the second metastable 4s'[1/2]0 (3P0, 1s3): no measurement located; theory 44.9 s (Small-Warren & Chiu 1975) stored.

Lifetimes of the resonance levels 4s[3/2]1 and 4s'[1/2]1 and of the 5s, 3d, 4d and the other 5p levels drawn: none located (5p[5/2]2 is now stored from Wiese et al. 1989) in an open source (Inoue, Setser, Sadeghi 1982 abstract: Ar(5p) lifetimes 100-140 ns, 5s and 3d about 50 ns, no level-resolved numbers).
Absolute (frequency-comb) frequencies of the 4s-4p lines: none located.

Primary papers behind the 4p lifetimes: Quadfasel & Helbig is listed as unpublished in Wiese et al. 1989, and Chang & Setser (J. Chem. Phys. 69, 3885 (1978)) is paywalled (Semantic Scholar: closed; no repository copy). Their numbers are stored second-hand from Wiese et al. Table II, which prints no uncertainties.

Volz & Schmoranzer beam-gas-laser lifetimes of Ar 4p levels: no open copy located (2 web searches, arXiv API, Semantic Scholar citation list of Wiese 1989; the open arXiv paper physics/0005057 that cites their method is about Kr). Not stored.

Welte et al., Rev. Sci. Instrum. 80, 113109 (2009): journal article not opened (not on arXiv); Welte's 2011 Heidelberg thesis (open) was read instead and gives slightly different final 39Ar constants, stored as alternatives.

Wiese et al. 1989 Table IV / VI (recommended A values of the 4s-4p and 4s-5p arrays) were not copied line by line: NIST ASD already carries this set and the site uses the NIST values. The scanned PDF is saved as data/literature/pdf/Ar_Wiese_1989.pdf if a line-by-line cross-check is wanted.
conflicts: 39Ar hyperfine A constants: Williams et al. 2011 [A(4s[3/2]2) = -285.36(13), A(4p[5/2]3) = -134.36(8) MHz] vs Welte et al. 2009 [-287.15(14), -135.16(12) MHz]: 1-2 MHz apart with ~0.1 MHz claimed uncertainties; the ratio A(4s)/A(4p) agrees to <0.1%. B constants agree. Williams (checked on 83Kr) is used.
g_J(4s[3/2]2): atomic-beam value 1.500964(8) (Lurio et al. 1960) vs 1.506 in NIST ASD (older optical value).

Keto & Kuo 1981 also assign 61 +- 10 ns to 3d'[3/2]1 (115366.866 cm^-1) and 61 +- 6 ns to 3d[3/2]1 (114147.732 cm^-1). Both are J = 1 resonance levels whose NIST A values to the ground state are 3.13e8 and 2.70e8 s^-1 (natural lifetime of a few ns), so the 61 ns figures are radiation-trapped cascade lifetimes at 2-3000 Torr and were NOT stored as level lifetimes.
Klose 1967 lifetimes of 2p1-2p4 carry 5-15 % systematic errors by the author's own estimate; treat as low-accuracy values.

4p lifetimes: Quadfasel & Helbig (laser-induced fluorescence, adopted by Wiese et al. 1989 and now the stored values) vs Chang & Setser 1978 differ by up to 13 % (2p4: 29.3 vs 33.2 ns; 2p3: 29.0 vs 27.6 ns; 2p6: 29.4 vs 27.0 ns). Klose 1967 (2p1 21, 2p2 25, 2p3 26, 2p4 31 ns) is 0-12 % lower/higher and was moved to the alternatives.

2p9 (811.5 nm upper level): 30.7 ns (Quadfasel & Helbig), 30.1 ns (Chang & Setser), 30.2 ns (Vassen review table = 1/A_NIST). Doery et al., Phys. Rev. A 57, 3603 (1998), Table VI print '33.1 ns' citing Wiese et al.; that number equals the Wiese/NIST A value 3.31e7 s^-1 read as a lifetime and was not stored.
5p[5/2]2 lifetime: 152(7) and 154(7) ns (Wiese et al. / Stryla et al., low pressure) vs 127(10) ns (Hirabayashi et al., high pressure).

39Ar hyperfine constants from Heidelberg: thesis values (Welte 2011: A_s = -285.9(0.14), A_p = -134.6(0.12) MHz) agree with Williams et al. within about 0.5 MHz, whereas the 2009 article values quoted by Williams (-287.15, -135.16) do not.
A(476.9, 487.6, 542.1 nm): de Regt et al. 1996 (7.40, 7.46, 7.33 x 10^5 s^-1, +-20 %) vs NIST ASD (8.6, 7.8, 6.0 x 10^5 s^-1, accuracy D-class); consistent within the uncertainties.
notes: Isotope-shift keys 'A-B' mean nu(A) - nu(B); heavier argon isotopes lie at higher frequency on 811.5 nm (Table III of Williams et al. is given relative to 38Ar: Delta nu(38,A') = nu(A') - nu(38)), while the 800.8 and 922.7 nm shifts of Chu et al. are printed relative to 40Ar. 39Ar and 37Ar are radioactive (ATTA tracers). Level energies are NIST ASD values from data/ar/levels.csv; Paschen names in the labels. Entries marked '(abstract)' were read on the publisher's abstract page only. Added 2026-10-01 (second pass): the 105 nm measurements of Velchev et al. are from 1999 (older than 20 years), so the NIST energy stays in use; isotope shifts of that line are printed as nu(40) - nu(A). Paschen-labelled lifetimes (Klose) were assigned to NIST levels by energy order. Added 2026-10-02 (third pass, papers opened in full): Wiese et al. 1989 (scanned PDF from the Max Planck repository; tables read from the page images), Klein et al. 1996 (CERN preprint scan), Welte's 2011 thesis, de Regt et al. 1996. Lifetimes of all ten 4p levels are second-hand (Quadfasel & Helbig unpublished, via Wiese Table II, no uncertainties printed). Isotope-shift entries of the 763.5 nm line carry the statistical error in 'unc' and the systematic one in 'unc_sys'. The rates A_s of the 5p[5/2]2 branches are R/tau from one paper, so tau x sum(A) = 1 by construction.
